name: Northeast Nigeria jihadist insurgency (ISWAP and Boko Haram)
started: 2009-07-26 (Boko Haram uprising; current phase marked by ISWAP's 2025-26 base offensive)
summary: ISWAP has spent 2025-26 overrunning Nigerian army bases in Borno and Yobe, killing several battalion commanders and adding armed drones to its arsenal, while its rival Boko Haram (JAS) has returned to suicide bombings in Maiduguri. The US entered the fight with Christmas 2025 strikes and a May 2026 raid that killed senior IS official Abu Bilal al-Minuki. The Lake Chad Basin saw 4,779 militant-linked deaths in 2025, 87% of them in Nigeria (Africa Center).

Nigerian Army Remotely Piloted Aircraft (NARPAS) Regiment

sides.name: Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP)

leaders: Abu Musab (leader, described as taking a wider regional role)
Abu Saleem (Wali of South Lake Chad, targeted 18 Oct 2026)

sides.name: Boko Haram (JAS)
members: Jama'atu Ahlis Sunna lid-Da'awati wal-Jihad, including the Lake Chad faction of Bakura Doro

background: Boko Haram's insurgency began in 2009. In 2016 it split: ISWAP, loyal to the Islamic State, built a disciplined proto-state around Lake Chad that taxes fishermen and farmers, while Abubakar Shekau's JAS kept its indiscriminate violence until Shekau died in 2021 fighting ISWAP. JAS survives in the Mandara mountains and the Lake Chad islands under Bakura Doro.

From 2025 ISWAP shifted to a campaign of night raids on army 'super camps' and forward bases, looting weapons and vehicles and filming the results. Why it matters: the strategy wears down Nigeria's ability to hold ground outside towns, keeps roads like Maiduguri-Damboa unsafe, and has drawn in Washington, whose politics around 'Christian genocide' now shape Nigeria's security relationship with the US.
year: In early November 2025 Bakura's JAS faction attacked ISWAP positions in Abadan and Kukawa with land and boat assaults (50-200 killed, ACLED). ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed an army brigadier-general near Wajiroko on 17 Nov 2025 (unverified). After President Trump designated Nigeria a country of particular concern and ordered the US military to prepare options, US forces struck IS targets in Sokoto state on 25 Dec 2025 in a joint operation with Nigeria.

ISWAP's base campaign intensified in January 2026: armed drones against troops in the Timbuktu Triangle, at least 20 soldiers killed at Malam-Fatori and an army major killed near Damasak on 23 Jan, and a drone attack on Sabon Gari base (11 killed) on 29 Jan. AFRICOM confirmed a small US team in Nigeria on 3 Feb. During Ramadan ISWAP raided bases at Mayanti (1 Mar), Konduga, Mainok, Jakana and Marte (5-6 Mar) and Kukawa and Goniri (9 Mar), killing two lieutenant colonels commanding battalions. JAS suicide bombers killed 23 in Maiduguri on 16 Mar, the fifth suicide attack of 2026. About 300 people were abducted at Ngoshe on 6 Mar. A Nigerian air strike on a Yobe market blamed on a misfire killed more than 100 on 11 Apr.

On 16 May a joint US-Nigerian operation killed Abu Bilal al-Minuki, head of IS's Al Furqan regional office, and AFRICOM struck again on 17 May. The same day militants killed at least 17 police trainees at the Special Forces school in Buni Yadi (Yobe). The US withdrew most deployed troops on 3 July while keeping intelligence support. Raids continued through mid-2026 (Gajiganna, Biu, Magumeri). From 10-18 Oct 2026 the army claimed seven air strikes killed 103 ISWAP fighters around Monguno and Guzamala and hit the residence of ISWAP's Wali of South Lake Chad.
situation: As of late October 2026 the army holds Maiduguri, the state capitals and garrison towns, but ISWAP dominates the Lake Chad shoreline and islands, the Timbuktu Triangle and parts of Sambisa, and continues to raid bases in northern Borno and Yobe. JAS remains active in the Mandara/Gwoza area and on Lake Chad, and fights ISWAP. US involvement has scaled down to intelligence support after the July withdrawal. The army is pressing an air campaign in Monguno and Guzamala LGAs.
technical: ISWAP armed-drone use: attacks on troops in the Timbuktu Triangle (mid-Jan 2026) and on Sabon Gari base (29 Jan 2026, at least 11 killed); Premium Times reported ISWAP acquired 35 drones via Lake Chad (ADF Magazine; Wikipedia).

Drone payloads are improvised: mortar bombs and grenades attached to commercial quadcopters (ADF Magazine). Nigeria counters with the domestic Damisa explosive drone and Lithuanian DM4S SkyWiper jammers.
ISWAP night raids on bases in a coordinated wave: Konduga (222 Battalion), Mainok and Jakana (5 Mar, about 22:30) and Marte (6 Mar, about 03:00); Lt. Col. S.I. Iliyasu killed (ICIR).

Commanders killed in 2026: an army major near Damasak (23 Jan); FOB commander Umar Ibrahim Mairiga at Mayanti (1 Mar); Lt. Col. Iliyasu at Konduga (5-6 Mar); Lt. Col. Umar Farouq at Kukawa (9 Mar) (ICIR).

JAS returned to suicide bombing in Maiduguri: three bombers hit the post office, Monday market and University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital gate on 16 Mar 2026 (23 killed); about 68 killed in Maiduguri over four months (ACLED).

JAS-ISWAP war: Bakura's JAS launched land and naval attacks on ISWAP in Abadan and Kukawa LGAs on 5-8 Nov 2025 (50-200 killed), despite an early-October truce; seven clashes recorded in early 2026 (ACLED).

US kinetic role: Christmas 2025 strikes (more than a dozen missiles, ship-launched per Pentagon video) in Sokoto; 16 May 2026 joint operation killed Abu Bilal al-Minuki and several other senior IS figures; 17 May AFRICOM strikes on militants on bicycles; US ISR flights from Ghana since late Nov 2025 (ACLED; LWJ; Stars and Stripes; AllAfrica/Reuters).
US footprint: AFRICOM confirmed a small team on 3 Feb 2026; reported as about 100 (Wikipedia) or about 200 (Stars and Stripes) trainers and intelligence enablers; most withdrawn 3 July 2026.

Nigerian air campaign, 10-18 Oct 2026: seven strikes by Army Aviation, the NARPAS drone regiment and other air assets including a 'Guardian' ISR asset; claimed 103 ISWAP killed, nine boat engines destroyed (army claim).
Air-strike errors: a market strike in Yobe on 11 Apr 2026 killed more than 100 (blamed on a misfire) (Wikipedia, 2026 in Nigeria).
ISWAP finance: ransoms, taxation and checkpoints enforced by mobile courts, cross-border smuggling, and loot from bases (HumAngle, cited in notes).
Abu Bilal al-Minuki's Al Furqan office oversaw IS activity in the Sahel, West and North Africa and Sudan; AFRICOM credited him with advising on drones and explosives (LWJ).
casualties: Africa Center (2025 data): Lake Chad Basin 4,779 militant-linked deaths (+28%), 87% in Nigeria (about 4,160), with battle deaths up 62%. ACLED: over 85% of Islamist-related incidents in Nigeria in 2025 were in the northeast. 2026 incidents include: Malam-Fatori 20+ soldiers (23 Jan), Sabon Gari 11 (29 Jan) and 25 workers (29-30 Jan), Maiduguri 23 (16 Mar), Yobe market air strike 100+ (11 Apr), Buni Yadi 17 police trainees (16 May). No rolling Oct 2025-Oct 2026 total found.
displaced: No current IDP totals were retrieved. Borno is closing IDP camps in Maiduguri without provision for new camps (HumAngle report on 2025 raids, noted for context).

timeline.event: JAS offensive against ISWAP in Abadan and Kukawa LGAs begins (50-200 killed).
ISWAP claims capture and killing of a brigadier-general near Wajiroko (unverified).
Mosque bombing in Maiduguri kills at least 7.
US strikes IS targets in Sokoto state jointly with Nigeria.
ISWAP attacks Malam-Fatori base (20+ soldiers killed).
ISWAP drone attack on Sabon Gari base kills at least 11.
AFRICOM confirms a US military team is in Nigeria.
ISWAP Ramadan raids on Konduga, Mainok, Jakana and Marte bases.
Triple suicide bombing in Maiduguri kills 23.
Nigerian air strike on a Yobe market kills more than 100 (misfire).
Joint US-Nigerian operation kills Abu Bilal al-Minuki; attack on Buni Yadi police school kills 17.
US withdraws most deployed forces; intelligence support continues.
Army strike on residence of ISWAP's Wali of South Lake Chad, Abu Saleem (army claim).

outlook: Watch whether ISWAP's drone and base-raid campaign resumes in the dry season, whether JAS suicide bombings in Maiduguri continue, whether the US resumes strikes after the July drawdown, and the ISWAP-JAS rivalry on Lake Chad. Mass-casualty air-strike errors remain a risk to the government's legitimacy.

zones.name: Lake Chad shore and islands (ISWAP core)
zones.note: ISWAP administrative heartland; Malam-Fatori, Kukawa, Monguno and Marte bases repeatedly attacked.

zones.name: Monguno-Guzamala
zones.note: Target of the Oct 2026 army air campaign (Badu, Arina Woje, Mairari, Gudumbali).

zones.name: Timbuktu Triangle and Sambisa Forest
zones.note: ISWAP and JAS forest bases; ISWAP drone attacks on advancing troops in Jan 2026.

zones.name: Maiduguri and Konduga ring
zones.note: State capital; JAS suicide bombings in 2026; Konduga, Mainok and Jakana bases raided in March.

zones.name: Mandara Mountains and Gwoza (JAS)
zones.note: Boko Haram (JAS) stronghold on the Cameroon border; Ngoshe abductions March 2026.

zones.name: Southern Yobe (Buni Yadi, Goniri)
zones.note: Buni Yadi Special Forces school attacked 16 May 2026; Goniri base raided 9 Mar.

battles.name: Nigerian air campaign in Monguno and Guzamala
battles.place: Badu, Arina Woje (Monguno LGA), Mairari, Gudumbali (Guzamala LGA), Borno; Duste Uku, Adamawa (mapped at Monguno)
sides: Nigerian Army Aviation, NARPAS regiment, air component
battles.outcome: Seven strikes; logistics hubs, boat engines and motorcycles destroyed (army claim).
battles.forces: Army Aviation, Remotely Piloted Aircraft regiment, a 'Guardian' ISR asset.
battles.losses: 103 ISWAP fighters killed (army claim, unverified), including about 30 at a gathering on 13 Oct; ISWAP Wali Abu Saleem's chief guard and a Shura member reported killed on 18 Oct.
battles.significance: The latest large Nigerian air operation in the window, targeting ISWAP's South Lake Chad leadership.

battles.name: US-Nigerian operation killing Abu Bilal al-Minuki
battles.place: Northeastern Nigeria, Lake Chad Basin (exact location not disclosed; coordinates approximate)
battles.outcome: Al-Minuki and several senior IS figures reported killed; follow-up AFRICOM strikes 17 May.
battles.forces: Joint US-Nigerian operation ordered by President Trump.
battles.losses: Al-Minuki and unnamed senior leaders (AFRICOM; IS has not confirmed).
battles.significance: Removed the head of IS's regional office for the Sahel, West and North Africa, possibly the head of its global provinces directorate; demonstrated a US kinetic role in Nigeria.

battles.name: ISWAP Ramadan raids on Borno and Yobe bases
battles.place: Mayanti, Konduga, Mainok, Jakana, Marte, Kukawa (Borno) and Goniri (Yobe), Nigeria; mapped at Konduga
battles.outcome: Several bases breached; army claimed 'scores' of militants killed; Goniri attack repelled.
battles.forces: Coordinated night attacks on at least six positions including the 222 Battalion at Konduga.
battles.losses: At least 14 soldiers killed on 4-5 Mar (Wikipedia); Lt. Col. S.I. Iliyasu (Konduga), Lt. Col. Umar Farouq (Kukawa) and FOB commander Umar Ibrahim Mairiga (Mayanti) killed; 12 soldiers and 3 civilians killed on 9 Mar.
battles.significance: Three unit commanders killed in about a week, a sign of ISWAP's ability to synchronise raids across the theatre.
